title: Add global error handler and graceful exit to CLI
description: Wrap the CLI's parseAsync call in a try/catch to handle unhandled errors gracefully. Also handle SIGINT (Ctrl+C) to exit cleanly without showing a stack trace to the user.
acceptanceCriteria: Unhandled errors show a user-friendly error message (not a raw stack trace)
Process exits with code 1 on unhandled errors
Pressing Ctrl+C during any command exits cleanly without a stack trace
SIGINT handler is registered before parseAsync is called

steps.description: Wrap parseAsync in try/catch in bin/rocket.ts
steps.details: In bin/rocket.ts, wrap the program.parseAsync call: `try { await program.parseAsync(process.argv) } catch (err) { const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err); console.error('\x1b[31mError:\x1b[0m', message); process.exit(1) }`
Before parseAsync, add: `process.on('SIGINT', () => { process.stdout.write('\n'); process.exit(0) })`. This intercepts Ctrl+C and exits cleanly.

Add: `process.on('unhandledRejection', (reason) => { const message = reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : String(reason); console.error('\x1b[31mUnhandled error:\x1b[0m', message); process.exit(1) })`
Temporarily modify a command handler to throw an error and verify: (1) error message is shown without stack trace, (2) process exits with code 1. Then test Ctrl+C exits cleanly.

technicalNotes: Use \x1b[31m...\x1b[0m for red color in error messages (ANSI escape codes) since chalk may not be set up at this point
Commander.js has its own error handling — set program.exitOverride() if you want to catch Commander errors in your try/catch
